name: MahuaShilp: Canopy-Net & NIR Rotary Micro-Dryer
pitch: Eliminating ground fires and dirt contamination in Bastar's 50,000-ton Mahua harvest through canopy nets and solar-thermal NIR rotary micro-dryers, doubling tribal farmgate realization.

problem.target_affected: Over 350,000 tribal families across Bastar Division who collect Mahua flowers (Madhuca longifolia) during March-May.
problem.frequency: Annual 6-8 week intensive harvest cycle.
problem.why_existing_fail: Gatherers deliberately burn dry Sal leaf litter beneath Mahua trees so fallen greenish-cream flowers can be spotted on ash. This triggers 60%+ of Bastar forest fires. Fallen flowers pick up soil, animal feces, and silica, while sun-drying on dirt tracks ferments sugars and breeds mycotoxins. Open sun-drying takes 4-5 days.
problem.consequence_if_unsolved: Destruction of forest biodiversity, severe respiratory hazard from smoke, and loss of 40-50% in farmgate selling price due to low grade (sold at ₹30-35/kg vs ₹70-80/kg for food-grade hygienic flowers).
evidence_and_sources: TRIFED Minor Forest Produce Annual Report 2024
Chhattisgarh State Minor Forest Produce Federation (CG MFP) Procurement Data
Bastar Forest Division Fire Incident Reports (March-May 2023-2025)

solution.description: A dual-stage system: (1) A lightweight ground-elevated tensioned poly-mesh canopy net that catches falling Mahua flowers without soil contact, eliminating leaf burning, and (2) A portable solar-assisted rotary drum micro-dryer with NIR moisture monitoring that cures flowers to <12% moisture in 6 hours.
hardware: Telescopic bamboo/aluminum perimeter frame
UV-stabilized 40-mesh monofilament netting
Perforated stainless steel rotary drum
12V 40W DC geared drive motor
PTC heating element with solar-thermal air pre-heater collector
ESP32 microcontroller
NIR reflectance optical sensor
software: Embedded PID thermal/moisture control firmware
Offline drying profile logger
Low-power BLE diagnostic app
ai_ml_iot: NIR spectral reflectance regression for moisture estimation
Adaptive PID drying curve algorithm to prevent caramelization of natural sugars

how_it_works.input_stage: Canopy catch net deployed around Mahua trunk; flowers drop directly onto clean mesh; gathered in clean bins without ground touching.
how_it_works.processing_stage: Flowers loaded into rotary drum micro-dryer; drum rotates at 12 RPM under regulated warm air stream (42°C-45°C).
how_it_works.decision_stage: Embedded NIR sensor measures water absorption band (1450nm) at regular drum cycles; micro-controller throttles airflow and drum speed.
how_it_works.action_stage: Automated buzzer and visual green LED activates when moisture reaches 11.5% target; heating cuts off to prevent over-drying.
how_it_works.output_stage: Golden-yellow, silica-free food-grade Mahua stored in hermetic bags; ready for premium brewery and confectionery sale.
how_it_works.ascii_diagram: [Falling Flowers] -> [Elevated Net] -> [Clean Hopper] -> [Rotary Drum (45°C)] -> [NIR Moisture Sensor] -> [Food-Grade Dry Mahua]

target_users.buyers: Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVKs), Large-sized Adivasi Multipurpose Societies (LAMPS), TRIFOOD Jagdalpur, and private food/craft beverage processors.
target_users.beneficiaries: Over 350,000 forest gatherers, Bastar Forest Department (fire reduction), and premium food/beverage consumers.

name: KodoClean: Centrifugal De-Huller & Air-Classifier for Small Millets
pitch: A low-power (0.5 HP) centrifugal rubber-rotor de-huller and vibratory air-classifier engineered specifically for tiny Kodo and Kutki grains, cutting broken grain losses from 35% to under 6%.

problem.target_affected: Over 120,000 small-millet (Kodo & Kutki) farmers across Bastar, Sukma, and Kanker districts, and regional millet processing units.
problem.frequency: Post-harvest processing cycle across 6 months annually.
problem.why_existing_fail: Chhattisgarh has declared itself the 'Millet Hub of India', but small millets (Kutki grain diameter ~1.5mm, Kodo ~2.0mm) have hard silicified 5-layer husks. Existing rice mills or heavy abrasive emery hullers crush Kutki, causing 30-40% grain breakage into unmarketable flour. Industrial millet mills cost ₹5-12 Lakhs and need 15 HP three-phase industrial power, unavailable in interior tribal hamlets.
problem.consequence_if_unsolved: Tribal farmers are forced to sell raw unhulled millets at MSP (₹30-40/kg) rather than processed edible grain (₹120-160/kg), losing 300% value capture.
evidence_and_sources: ICAR-IIMR (Indian Institute of Millets Research) Small Millet Processing Bulletin
Chhattisgarh State Millet Mission Progress Report 2024
Bastar District Agriculture Department Millet Baseline Survey

solution.description: A single-phase / solar-compatible 0.5 HP centrifugal impact de-huller with variable-gap vulcanized elastomer impact rings, integrated with a counter-current vibratory pneumatic air-classifier that separates husk from whole grains in a single continuous pass.
hardware: 0.5 HP BLDC 24V motor
Conical polyurethane rotor with radial acceleration channels
Replaceable vulcanized silicone-rubber impact stator ring
Eccentric vibratory screen deck (dual sieve 1.2mm / 1.8mm)
Aspiration cyclone fan with transparent husk chamber
ESP32-S3 motor controller with load current sensing
software: Adaptive motor RPM controller based on moisture and grain variety preset (Kodo vs Kutki vs Ragi)
Digital throughput logger
ai_ml_iot: Current-signature analysis to prevent rotor choking and automatically regulate grain feeding hopper gate via stepper motor

how_it_works.input_stage: Raw unhulled Kutki/Kodo poured into top vibrating feed hopper; stepper-actuated gate regulates flow.
how_it_works.processing_stage: Grains drop into high-speed centrifugal conical rotor; flung tangentially against resilient rubber impact ring; husk shears off due to differential deceleration without shattering the inner starch kernel.
how_it_works.decision_stage: Current sensor monitors BLDC load torque; adjusts feeder vibration to maintain peak 25 kg/hr throughput.
how_it_works.action_stage: Mixture drops across vibratory sieves while an upward cyclonic airflow lifts light husks into collection cyclone.
how_it_works.output_stage: Whole polished edible millet grain discharges into clean chute; broken grain <6%; husks collected separately for bio-briquettes.
how_it_works.ascii_diagram: [Unhulled Millet] -> [Auto-Feed Gate] -> [Centrifugal Rubber Rotor] -> [Pneumatic Air Lift] -> [Vibratory Deck] -> [Intact Whole Grain]

name: BodaShield: Evaporative-Chilled N2 Pod for Wild Mushrooms
pitch: A portable solar-battery backpack preservation pod combining Peltier-zeolite chilling and micro-nitrogen purging, extending the transit shelf-life of Bastar's ₹2,000/kg wild Boda mushrooms from 24 hours to 8 days.

problem.target_affected: Forest tribals who forage wild Boda (Termitomyces spp.) mushrooms under Sal trees, and regional fresh-produce traders.
problem.frequency: Intense 4-week window during initial monsoon rains (June-July).
problem.why_existing_fail: Boda is an underground mycorrhizal mushroom that is considered an exquisite culinary delicacy, fetching ₹1,200 to ₹2,200/kg in Jagdalpur and Raipur. However, Boda has extreme post-harvest cellular respiration. Within 24-36 hours, it sweats, turns black, liquefies, and rots. Ice packs freeze-burn the outer cuticle, while conventional cold rooms are miles away from dense forest collection points.
problem.consequence_if_unsolved: Tribal gatherers are forced to distress-sell Boda to intermediaries for ₹300-400/kg; over 60% of harvested Boda spoils before reaching high-paying urban markets like Raipur, Hyderabad, or Delhi.
evidence_and_sources: ICAR-DMR (Directorate of Mushroom Research) Post-Harvest Bulletin
Bastar Mandi Price Bulletin (June-July 2024)
Journal of Forest Products and Tribal Economy Research on Termitomyces

solution.description: A ruggedized, insulated 15 kg backpack pod featuring active thermoelectric (Peltier) chilling maintained at 6°C, integrated with an on-demand zeolite micro-pressure swing adsorption (PSA) cartridge that flushes the chamber with 95% nitrogen, halting enzymatic browning and microbial respiration.
hardware: Vacuum-insulated panel / EPP composite backpack enclosure
Dual TEC1-12706 Peltier cooling modules with heat-pipe sinks
12V 20Ah LiFePO4 battery pack with 40W foldable solar panel
Miniature 12V diaphragm air pump with synthetic zeolite 13X column
Sensirion SHT31 Temp/RH sensor
NDIR CO2 and O2 sensor
ESP32 telemetry board with BLE
software: Controlled atmosphere preservation firmware
BLE mobile app showing real-time freshness index and chamber parameters
GPS breadcrumb logger for foraging traceability
ai_ml_iot: Kinetic respiration degradation model predicting remaining shelf-life hours based on time-temperature-gas integral

how_it_works.processing_stage: Lid sealed; user presses 'Purge'; miniature pump draws ambient air through zeolite column, exhausting O2 and flooding chamber with dry N2 until O2 < 3%.
how_it_works.decision_stage: Temperature sensor triggers Peltier circuit to maintain stable 6°C (+/- 1°C); RH maintained at 85% without condensation.
how_it_works.action_stage: Low-power micro-controller sleeps, waking every 10 minutes to verify gas hermeticity and temperature stability.
how_it_works.output_stage: Mushrooms remain firm, fragrant, and pristine for 8 days; enables inter-state express cold cargo delivery to luxury restaurants across India.

name: TamarindIQ: Optical-Dielectric Slab Deseeding & Moisture Grader
pitch: A non-destructive optical-transmission and RF-dielectric scanner for compressed tamarind slabs in Jagdalpur Mandi, detecting embedded seeds, moisture fraud, and foreign dirt in 5 seconds.

problem.target_affected: Tamarind gatherers, rural processing SHGs, Mandi commission agents, and wholesale spice exporters in Jagdalpur (Asia's largest tamarind aggregation hub).
problem.frequency: Year-round trading with peak procurement from February to May.
problem.why_existing_fail: Jagdalpur Mandi trades over 30,000 metric tons of tamarind annually. Traded tamarind is pressed into 1kg and 20kg sticky black slabs. Dishonest intermediaries spray water into slabs to increase weight by 20-30% (causing inner mold rot) and leave 15-20% broken seed fragments inside supposedly 'deseeded' slabs. Currently, Mandi inspectors manually stab slabs with a needle or cut random corners—a subjective, destructive method leading to disputes and unfair discounting of honest tribal gatherers.
problem.consequence_if_unsolved: Over ₹50 Crores in trade disputes, massive rejection of Indian tamarind consignments in Middle Eastern/European export ports due to aflatoxins, and chronic exploitation of tribal processors.
evidence_and_sources: Spices Board of India Tamarind Export Quality Standard Directives
Jagdalpur Krishi Upaj Mandi Tamarind Trade Register 2024
TRIFED Bastar Tamarind Processing Cluster Study

solution.description: A benchtop inspection station utilizing dual-frequency capacitive fringing-field dielectric sensors (for core volumetric moisture) combined with a high-intensity multi-wavelength NIR optical transillumination grid (for internal seed density mapping), producing an instant digital Grade Certificate.
hardware: High-power 850nm/940nm pulsed LED transillumination array
High-sensitivity monochrome NIR line-scan camera
Dual-frequency (100kHz & 10MHz) planar capacitive fringing-field sensor plates
ESP32-S3 microcontroller with edge DSP
Raspberry Pi 4 for computer vision processing
Thermal receipt printer for instant Mandi grade slips
software: OpenCV edge detection and blob contour analysis for embedded seed shadow detection
Dielectric calibration algorithm mapping capacitance/dissipation factor directly to moisture percentage
Mandi cloud sync / e-NAM API connector
ai_ml_iot: Trained lightweight CNN (MobileNetV2) classifying slab defect score: seed contamination, moisture level, mold void detection

name: KosaSort: Opto-Acoustic Silk Cocoon Sexing & Deflossing Machine
pitch: A gentle non-destructive opto-acoustic sexing and motorized deflossing station for Bastar's wild Kosa (Tasar) silk cocoons, increasing grainage reproductive efficiency by 40% and saving 25% silk peduncle waste.

problem.why_existing_fail: Bastar Kosa silk (Antheraea mylitta) is world-renowned for its golden luster and durability. In seed grainages (breeding stations), rearers must separate male and female live pupae inside hard outdoor cocoons to synchronize moth emergence for disease-free egg (DFL) laying. Currently, rearers manually cut a window into the cocoon shell with a razor—destroying the continuous silk filament and killing 15-20% of pupae through accidental incisions. Furthermore, manual deflossing (stripping fuzzy outer floss) is grueling and tears the outer silk layer.

Confirming with Gold Standard HPLC (High Performance Liquid Chromatography) requires sending venous blood vials to Raipur or Jagdalpur Medical College, taking 3-4 weeks for reports with huge loss-to-follow-up.

pitch: A fail-safe active-passive hybrid cold-chain backpack carrier for remote primary health centers, combining 4°C solid-solid phase change materials with solar/12V Peltier heat-pumping and Bluetooth temperature breach logging to keep snakebite antivenom potent during 18-hour monsoonal power outages.

Remote SHCs face 12 to 24-hour power outages during monsoon storms. name: FerroClear: Catalytic Siphon-Aerated Iron Remediation Filter
pitch: A zero-electricity, community-scale catalytic aeration and pyrolusite filtration system with automatic siphon backwash, eliminating toxic iron (>8.0 mg/L) from tribal school borewells for under ₹15,000.

problem.frequency: Daily continuous drinking water contamination.
problem.why_existing_fail: Bastar and Dantewada sit on massive hematite iron ore formations (e.g., Bailadila ranges). Consequently, deep groundwater has dangerous geogenic iron concentrations ranging from 3.0 to 12.0 mg/L (far exceeding the BIS IS-10500 safe limit of 0.3 mg/L). Consuming this water causes chronic constipation, gastrointestinal distress, organ damage, and dental staining, while turning midday meals black and encrusting school water pipes. Existing government iron removal plants (IRPs) fail within 3 months because: (a) they require chemical dosing (bleach/potassium permanganate) which village schools never replenish, and (b) they clog up because no one performs manual valve backwashing.
problem.consequence_if_unsolved: Hundreds of thousands of tribal schoolchildren poisoned by toxic iron levels; schools abandoning clean tap water schemes to drink dirty open stream water.

solution.description: A completely gravity-powered, chemical-free, zero-electricity iron filtration unit. It utilizes a high-efficiency Venturi-vortex aspirator that vigorously oxygenates incoming borewell water (oxidizing soluble ferrous Fe2+ to insoluble ferric Fe3+), followed by a multi-media catalytic bed of naturally active pyrolusite (manganese dioxide ore) coated quartz sand that accelerates catalytic iron precipitation, coupled with a clever automatic bell-siphon that self-backwashes the filter bed automatically when head loss peaks, flushing iron sludge without manual valves.

name: ConveyorGuard: Self-Powered Acoustic-Thermal Bearing Watcher
pitch: A battery-free wireless vibration and infrared sensor puck magnetically attached to overland ore conveyor idlers at NMDC Nagarnar Steel and Bailadila mines, detecting bearing cage failure and preventing ₹5-Crore belt friction fires.

problem.why_existing_fail: Overland conveyor systems transport millions of tons of heavy iron ore across 5 to 15 kilometers of rugged terrain. The moving rubber belt rubs against the stationary jammed steel roller, generating friction temperatures exceeding 400°C. Within minutes, the rubber belt ignites, destroying kilometers of expensive steel-cord belt, shutting down the entire blast furnace or ore plant (costing ₹2-5 Crores per incident). Manual human inspection with handheld pyrometers across 10 km in dust and rain is hazardous, infrequent, and catches bearings only after they are already failing.
problem.consequence_if_unsolved: Catastrophic plant shutdown, millions of dollars in equipment damage, and severe burn injuries to mining personnel.

It operates battery-free by harvesting waste energy from idler mechanical vibration (piezoelectric cantilever) and heat differential (thermoelectric generator - TEG). The node continuously monitors bearing acoustic emission and surface temperature via non-contact infrared thermopiles. An ultra-low-power edge DSP processor runs vibration FFTs to detect early bearing raceway micro-cracks (BPFO/BPFI frequencies) weeks before seizure, broadcasting alerts over an industrial wireless mesh network.

name: DhokraFurnace: Clean Gas Recuperative Foundry Kiln for Bell-Metal
pitch: A portable ceramic-fiber insulated recuperative gas-fired melting kiln for Bastar's world-famous Dhokra bell-metal artisans, cutting melting time from 5 hours to 45 minutes, slashing fuel costs by 60%, and eliminating toxic indoor smoke.

problem.target_affected: Over 5,000 indigenous Dhokra (lost-wax brass casting) and bell-metal artisan families in Bastar (Kondagaon, Tokapal, Bastar village).
problem.frequency: Daily continuous metal casting production.
problem.why_existing_fail: Bastar's Dhokra art (dating back 4,000 years to the Mohenjo-daro Dancing Girl) is a GI-tagged heritage craft. However, artisans still melt brass and bronze scrap in primitive open-pit charcoal furnaces powered by manual foot bellows. Achieving brass melting temperatures (950°C-1,000°C) takes 4 to 6 hours of grueling labor, consuming massive amounts of expensive wood charcoal (₹30-35/kg). Up to 40% of heat is lost to the atmosphere, while artisan families—including children—inhale thick, toxic carbon monoxide, metal fumes, and smoke, causing rampant chronic bronchitis and eye cataracts. Furthermore, uneven open-pit heating causes high casting porosity and mold breakage, resulting in a 25% product rejection rate.
problem.consequence_if_unsolved: Gradual extinction of an ancient world-heritage craft as younger generations abandon the grueling, unhealthy trade; acute respiratory illness in artisan communities.

The kiln uses a lightweight refractory ceramic fiber (RCF) and alumina-silicate lining (withstanding 1,300°C) with an innovative counter-flow waste heat recuperator that pre-heats incoming combustion air using escaping flue gases. Fueled by clean domestic/commercial LPG or biogas via a tuned Venturi ribbon burner with digital pyrometric temperature monitoring, it melts 5 kg of brass in just 45 minutes at 60% lower fuel cost with zero soot or toxic smoke.

When visiting Fair Price ration shops or Gram Panchayat offices, tribals are routinely cheated by corrupt intermediaries who under-weigh grain rations or skim MGNREGA wage payments. name: MadhuShodhan: Low-Temp Solar Vacuum Thin-Film Honey Dehydrator
pitch: A gentle low-temperature (under 40°C) solar-thermal rotary vacuum thin-film dehydrator for Bastar's wild forest honey, reducing moisture from 25% to FSSAI-compliant <18% without destroying bioactive enzymes or darkening color.

problem.target_affected: Over 15,000 tribal honey hunters and Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVKs) gathering wild forest honey (Apis dorsata) in Bastar.
problem.frequency: Two main harvesting cycles: Summer (Chaitra) and Post-Monsoon (Kartik).
problem.why_existing_fail: Bastar wild forest honey (harvested from giant rock bees, Apis dorsata) is prized for rich medicinal properties and unique floral nectar. However, fresh wild honey harvested in tropical forests has an inherently high moisture content (23% to 26%). According to FSSAI standards, commercial honey must have moisture <20% (ideally <18%); above 20%, natural osmotolerant wild yeasts ferment the honey into sour alcohol and vinegar within 3 months, bursting containers. Existing commercial honey processing plants use high-temperature thermal pasteurizers (heating honey to 65°C-75°C). This ruins raw forest honey: it destroys delicate heat-sensitive enzymes (diastase, invertase), spikes toxic HMF (hydroxymethylfurfural) levels, and turns golden wild honey black, destroying its premium export value.
problem.consequence_if_unsolved: Tribal gatherers are forced to sell fresh honey at distress prices (₹150-180/kg); millions of liters ferment and spoil; loss of export market access.

A rotating stainless-steel disc rotor continuously spreads honey into ultra-thin liquid films inside the vacuum chamber, accelerating moisture extraction down to 17.5% in 2 hours while preserving 100% of live enzymes, natural pollen, and delicate floral aromas.

name: BioFlex-Socket: Rapid Heat-Molded Modular Transtibial Prosthetic
pitch: A modular, low-temperature thermoformable and ratchet-lacing adjustable transtibial prosthetic socket system, allowing a technician to custom-fit below-knee amputees in remote Bastar villages in under 2 hours for <₹3,500.

problem.target_affected: Over 4,500 lower-limb amputees across the Bastar conflict corridor and rural farming belts (victims of landmines/IED blasts, road accidents, and agricultural thresher machinery injuries).
problem.frequency: Permanent daily mobility requirement.
problem.why_existing_fail: Conventional prosthetic sockets (like Jaipur Foot polypropylene or Western laminated carbon sockets) require plaster-of-paris negative mold casting, positive mold pouring, and vacuum thermoforming. In Bastar, amputees must travel 300 km over rough terrain to Raipur or Jagdalpur district hospital, wait 3 to 4 weeks for socket fabrication, and spend ₹25,000 to ₹50,000. Furthermore, rural amputees experience dramatic stump volume fluctuations (swelling in monsoons, atrophy during heavy manual labor). A rigid plaster-cast socket becomes loose or causes agonizing pressure ulcers within months, forcing rural amputees to abandon their prostheses and crawl or use wooden crutches.
problem.consequence_if_unsolved: Complete economic destitution, loss of livelihood, severe depression, and lifelong immobility for rural youth and blast survivors.
evidence_and_sources: National Institute for the Locomotor Disabilities (NILD) Rehabilitation Studies
District Disability Rehabilitation Centre (DDRC) Bastar Annual Patient Registry

solution.description: A breakthrough, modular, adjustable transtibial (below-knee) prosthetic socket system. The socket is composed of interlocking segmented struts made of a low-temperature thermo-formable composite (which softens at 65°C in warm water and can be molded directly onto the patient's stump over a silicone liner in 15 minutes without plaster casts). It incorporates a micro-adjustable steel-cable dial lacing system (Boa/ratchet dial) that allows the amputee to expand or tighten the socket volume instantly throughout the day as their stump fluctuates, connected to a standard universal 4-hole prosthetic pylon adapter.
